name: Carbonate / bicarbonate equilibrium (acid-base speciation; pH + charge)

provenance.ref: Aquatic Chemistry: carbonate system pK1=6.35, pK2=10.33 (freshwater, 25C)

notes: An acid/base speciation and pH box. Each formula carries the species' actual protonation, so bicarbonate (HCO3-, 1 H) and carbonate (CO3--, 0 H) stay distinct rather than both collapsing to H2CO3; the ChEBI entity_id is the identity that distinguishes them, and charge is a first-class facet so the reactions are charge-balance verified, not only mass. The forward/reverse ratios reproduce the measured equilibrium constants (kf1/kr1 = Ka1 = 10^-6.35 M, kf2/kr2 = Ka2 = 10^-10.33 M); reverse rates set a nominal relaxation timescale, so the equilibrium speciation and the resulting pH (about 4.2 for CO2-saturated water) are physically grounded. Closed and atom- plus charge-balanced by construction.

validity.note: mass-action relaxation to carbonate equilibrium; illustrative rate constants. Aqueous, dilute.
